      • triggerProcessing

        public void triggerProcessing​(@NotNull
                              @NotNull ReleaseChangeEvent event)
        Description copied from interface: ReleaseChangeProcess
        Adds the information about the event into an internal queue. Shouldn't throw any exceptions and not do anything risky - the actual processing is done when #run() is called. If there is anything to do and run should be triggered, the ReleaseChangeProcess.getState() should be switched to ReleaseChangeProcess.ReleaseChangeProcessorState.awaiting. The caller guarantees that #run() is called soon.
        Specified by:
        triggerProcessing in interface ReleaseChangeProcess

      • runReplication

        public void runReplication()
        Description copied from interface: ReleaseChangeProcess
        This method performs the actual replication processing. This is meant to be automatically called from the internal release change publishing mechanism (specifically ReleaseChangeEventPublisherImpl, not a part of the GUI.

        The contract with the ReleaseChangeEventPublisherImpl is: it calls this method after changes to the release have been received, e.g. by entering the ReleaseChangeProcess into a threadpool. Must not be called twice in parallel. If there is nothing in the queue, this should just be a no-op.

        Specified by:
        runReplication in interface ReleaseChangeProcess

      • abort

        public void abort()
        Description copied from interface: ReleaseChangeProcess
        If the process is currently running, this triggers an abort. Caution: this might take a while since the currently running operation might have to be finished / resources might need to be cleared up. If the process is stopped, it resets the state to ReleaseChangeProcess.ReleaseChangeProcessorState.idle to allow "acknowledging" an error.
        Specified by:
        abort in interface ReleaseChangeProcess
